Sometimes it takes a while for a travel brand to make itself known. There have been whispers about the loveliness of the North East coast above Tynemouth for a while, but it was only in 2025 that Hazel Plater, a local photographer, christened her long-form documentary photo-project “The Geordie Riviera”.

“I love the region, which has so much to offer, and I think is underappreciated nationally,” she told local media. “At the same time, though, I don’t want too many people to know about our unspoilt beaches!”
Good luck with that one. This year the nickname has been picked up by national newspapers, and anyway, Dan Jackson, a local author, was already plugging the “Northumbrian Riviera” back in 2022.
But does it live up to the billing? And can it challenge the sultrier southern coasts?
Below, we have awarded each of Britain’s would-be rivieras a mark out of 10 for “riviera-ness”. Which is your favourite?
### The Yorkshire Riviera

[![Redcar Steelworks at sunset from the coast path near Saltburn-by-the-Sea](https://hermes.media.static.aol.com/media/2026/09/24/be3c23ca-f96c-3594-b0d8-ad2214f05261/2b8561ea-9e30-44bd-8da4-a1c8e3ed040e.jpeg)](https://hermes.media.static.aol.com/media/2026/09/24/be3c23ca-f96c-3594-b0d8-ad2214f05261/2b8561ea-9e30-44bd-8da4-a1c8e3ed040e.jpeg)
Redcar sits at the heart of the Yorkshire Riviera - Andrew Ray/Alamy

An 18-minute amateur film by Raymond Kitching shot in 1958 was titled _Yorkshire Riviera_ – so the handle has been around for some time. It opens with a view of the South Gare breakwater at Teesmouth from Coatham beach, and covers the North Yorkshire coast from Redcar to [Scarborough](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/travel/destinations/europe/united-kingdom/england/yorkshire/north/scarborough/why-visit-scarborough-uk/). A more recent source plots the riviera from Redcar through Bridlington to Withernsea.

So while no one doubts the attractiveness or historic value of Scarborough and [Whitby](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/travel/news/classic-british-seaside-town-whitby/), there can’t be a riviera if no one knows where it is. Maybe there’s a joke implied, that no self-respecting bluff Yorkshireman would have any truck with foreign words such as “riviera”.

### The Geordie Riviera

Cullercoats Beach is a sheltered beach with golden sands - Owen Humphreys/PA Archive

Tynemouth’s greatest asset is Long Sands Beach, which is a mile long and backed by dunes; it has a food festival and restaurant festival and was ranked Britain’s second-best seaside town in the most recent _Which?_ survey.

Cullercoats is good for paddleboarding and bathing. Whitley Bay is a small resort town with a lighthouse and a former concert hall and much-loved landmark called Spanish City (mentioned in Dire Straits’ _Tunnel of Love_).
